brief:
Israeli opposition parties are pledging to shift the country's political direction, yet their platforms diverge little from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's on core issues, Al Jazeera English reported. Parties opposing Netanyahu's government have not clearly differentiated themselves on key policy matters, raising questions about the substance of promised political change.

The opposition's campaign messaging emphasizes a break from Netanyahu's tenure, but concrete policy differences remain unclear to voters. Political observers question whether the choice presented to Israeli voters represents a genuine ideological shift or merely a personnel change within the broader right-wing consensus.
dek: Benjamin Netanyahu’s opponents are promising a change to Israeli politics, but are their policies really that different?
title: Netanyahu's rivals offer limited alternative to Israeli right-wing politics
